title: Agentic AI Summit 2026 — local evidence analysis
cutoff_note: Accepted corpus cutoff; Aug-2 remained live/incomplete in the evidence snapshot.
scope: Authorized local evidence only; no network research or external action in this candidate build.

summary.conclusion: The clearest technical through-line is an agent system stack: harness + memory/tools + execution + feedback + scalable environments, with scientific discovery and security as adjacent application/risk layers.
summary.fact_boundary: Aug-1 transcript evidence is auto-caption-derived. Aug-2 has six unavailable transcript entries; River photos and company notes are labeled separately.
summary.interpretation_boundary: Jason-fit and job/collaboration leads are analysis, not facts or recommendations to contact/apply.

claims.label: fact
claims.statement: The Atlas morning talk frames agentic modeling as turning a language model from a talker into a doer, coupled to an agent harness.
claims.speaker_session_mapping: Atlas / Session 1: Foundational Capabilities; speaker-level attribution withheld because the ASR self-introduction is noisy.
claims.attribution_confidence: medium — schedule-to-stream stage mapping; auto transcript; no speaker named in this claim

evidence.excerpt: agentic modeling is the process where we want to turn this talker to a doer
evidence.excerpt_note: Normalized English auto transcript; ASR artifacts are preserved in the excerpt.

claims.label: fact
claims.statement: The same talk describes an information layer with memory, context management, and tools, plus an execution layer with prompt/action modules and error recovery.
claims.speaker_session_mapping: Atlas / Session 1: Foundational Capabilities; stage/session only.
claims.attribution_confidence: medium — stage-to-session schedule mapping; auto transcript

evidence.excerpt: the information layer consists of the uh ma memory and the context measurement
evidence.excerpt_note: Normalized English auto transcript; this is an excerpt, not a polished transcript.

claims.label: fact
claims.statement: The talk presents EvolveLab as a test-time learning framework intended to accumulate and reuse knowledge across a sequence of tasks.
claims.speaker_session_mapping: Atlas / Session 1: Foundational Capabilities; stage/session only.
claims.attribution_confidence: medium — stage-to-session schedule mapping; auto transcript

evidence.excerpt: a new test time learning framework called evolve lab which allows large scale language models to accumulate, reuse and involve knowledge across a sequence of tasks
evidence.excerpt_note: The normalized transcript renders some words as ASR artifacts (for example, ‘involve’).

claims.label: fact
claims.statement: The talk identifies a need for environments that can run very large numbers of agents in parallel to produce trajectory data for training.
claims.speaker_session_mapping: Atlas / Session 1: Foundational Capabilities; stage/session only.
claims.attribution_confidence: medium — stage-to-session schedule mapping; auto transcript

evidence.excerpt: to run hundreds of thousands of uh agents simultaneously so that they can generate a lot of trajectory data
evidence.excerpt_note: Normalized English auto transcript; quantity is reported as spoken, not independently measured.
